narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated an 80% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In this admissions process, that high predicted risk was treated as reason enough to reject your application, since the school uses likely bar success as a key condition for admission.

The prediction was driven most strongly by your LSAT score, then by your third-year class standing, and then by your first-year class standing. Each of these factors pushed the estimate toward bar failure rather than success. Your LSAT score of 19 is far below the average of about 37 among accepted students, making it the single strongest warning signal. Your third-year decile of 1 means you were in the lowest tenth of your class, compared with an accepted-student average near 6; this was the second strongest factor and also pointed toward failure. Your first-year decile of 1, again far below the accepted average near 6, was the third most influential factor and reinforced the same concern. Your gender and race were not used in this prediction.

To improve future chances, ask admissions whether any reconsideration or feedback is available, and meet with a pre-law advisor. Focus first on preparing for and retaking the LSAT, since it was the largest factor. Also seek guidance on strengthening your academic record or explaining your early class standing, and consider delaying reapplication or applying to programs that review candidates more holistically.
